prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-04-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-04-29):
| Current ratio           | 1.39 |
| Retained earnings       | 49,956M |
| Current liabilities     | 18,377M |
| Current assets          | 25,508M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 52,061M |
| Total liabilities       | 57,728M |
| Total assets            | 110,429M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,842M |
| Revenue                 | 11,164M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid liquidity with a current ratio of 1.39 and reasonable asset/liability balance (total assets 110.4B vs. total liabilities 57.7B). Equity cushion is meaningful (shareholders’ equity 52.1B) alongside EBIT of 1.84B on revenue 11.16B, suggesting decent earnings capacity to service debt, though debt levels are moderate relative to equity. Overall, credit risk appears to be in the investment-grade range without strong disruption indicators, supporting a BBB+ assessment.

DECISION: BBB+
